source.title: Statistical generalization performance guarantee for meta-learning with data dependent prior
source.authors: Tianyu Liu; Jie Lu; Zheng Yan; Guang-Quan Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, but its title is “PAC-Bayes Bounds for Meta-learning with Data-Dependent Prior,” which differs from the provided title.
record.tranche_reason: Reports generalization results for stochastic meta-learning on permuted MNIST task environments, extending the topic to a different setting. It does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test error, test loss, and PAC-Bayes bounds for meta-learning objectives. The table values are retained as findings about meta-learning generalization; they do not measure the natural-label versus random-label generalization gap in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study cites Exploring Generalization in Deep Learning but tests PAC-Bayes meta-learning objectives and prior choices, not V1–V8. Label permutations define consistent classification tasks rather than independently randomized example labels. FCN and CNN results use different task environments, so they do not test architectural advantage. Adam and batch size are fixed; weight variance is not evaluated as a predictor of generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Section VII: the authors conclude that the λ and variational objectives provide competitive bounds and estimation accuracy in both MNIST environments, and that data-dependent priors accelerate convergence. This is their conclusion, not evidence of uniformly improved final test accuracy; shuffled-pixel test errors are higher with data-dependent priors.
record.recipe_differences: Stochastic meta-learning with PAC-Bayes training objectives and data-dependent priors; evaluates permuted MNIST tasks rather than the listed natural-label/random-label capacity and generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test errors differ by MNIST environment, prior type, and training objective.

fits_no_version.finding: On shuffled-pixel MNIST tasks, reported test errors are 2.432–2.832% with random priors and 3.614–4.033% with data-dependent priors across the five objectives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested stochastic FCN meta-learning setting, prior configuration and PAC-Bayes training objective affect held-out task performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On permuted-label MNIST tasks, reported test errors are 40.73–55.60% with random priors and 0.882–0.950% with data-dependent priors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested stochastic CNN meta-learning setting, data-dependent-prior recipes yield substantially lower held-out task error than random-prior recipes.

record.problems: The experiments cover only two MNIST task environments and stochastic meta-learning. The supplied results do not compare training and test error using the same metric, and therefore do not directly measure a generalization gap. The permuted-label test errors with random prior are large and variable, while data-dependent-prior values are much lower; the text does not explain this difference in the supplied tables.
record.rows_left_out: Table II also reports test bound and test loss for the same conditions; omitted because the 20 test-error rows capture the primary held-out accuracy metric. Table I training-phase measures and other figure results are not extracted because they do not provide a comparable training-test error gap.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting and natural-label generalization with the same architecture and recipe, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched CNN–FCN comparisons and the contributions of local connectivity, learned sparsity, or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as a predictor of generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text identifies itself as arXiv:2102.03748, PAC-Bayes Bounds for Meta-learning with Data-Dependent Prior; its correspondence to the supplied DOI cannot be established from this message. All 20 test-error values and confidence intervals match Table II. The prior comparison includes additional ERM prior training on 30% of each task's training data, including prior construction for new tasks; it is a comparison of recipes, not an isolated prior substitution.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization alongside natural-label test generalization.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on the listed image benchmarks.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons under the stated tuning regimes.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the test-accuracy effect.
